scientific_question: Does the published start-phase/stopover relation persist within deer conditional on calendar departure day, individual and year effects?
sampling: Exactly same complete-case repeated-animal observations admitted in PR #413: n=100, 38 deer, eight observation years, true zero durations preserved, 25 original missing rows never zero-imputed.
predictor: DFP_Start; positive = calendar departure later relative to origin green-up peak; constructed retrospectively and NOT known animal cue
calendar_covariate: DOY_Start; actual departure day of year
endpoint: whole-route observed stopover.day; no DFP_End, travel speed, total travel time, reproduction
primary_model: stopover_it = individual FE + year FE + beta_calendar * DOY_Start_it + beta_phase * DFP_Start_it + error_it
target_estimand: Conditional within-individual linear beta_phase (stopover days per DFP day), not causal cue-use
null_model: stopover_it = individual FE + year FE + beta_calendar * DOY_Start_it + error_it
expected_phase_sign: negative; failure to retain a negative confidence interval is not a confirmation of phenological cue use or its absence
estimation: FWL residualize animal and year fixed effects, then separately residualize DFP on actual DOY; no categorical timing bins or post-hoc alternative equations.

uncertainty.method: whole-animal histories cluster bootstrap with resampled animal labels

supplementary: Residual SSE difference vs calendar-only on same n; show partial VIF and all source support counts. No out-of-sample performance claimed.
constraints: Do not select other covariates or change support gates after coefficients
No original animal identifiers or source rows committed
follow_up_if_support_fails: Report NOT_ESTIMABLE; record collinearity/design stats only, no phase-effect fit, no threshold lowering.
